title: KV cache eviction pressure extract — incident data pull
body:
Purpose:
Pull raw telemetry and event traces to quantify the impact of heightened KV cache evictions on regional GPU queueing and token throttles during the 2026-11-15 incident window. This sheet captures the queries used, field definitions, example slices, and quick visualizable aggregates for the postmortem write-up.

Summary (short):
- Incident window: 2026-11-15 02:10 UTC -> 2026-11-15 06:45 UTC
- Primary symptom: sudden spike in per-request latency and token-level throttles in us-west1 and eu-central1, correlating with increased KV cache evictions and reduced effective batch sizes.
- Immediate impact: 6% request failure due to soft throttles, median p95 latency up ~3x for long-context requests.

High-level hypothesis:
A rolling change to the cache-retention policy in the serving runtime (PR 2245) reduced in-memory prefix retention for long context sessions. This increased cold KV cache miss rate, which led to more frequent KV recompute work per request and pressure on GPU scheduling queues. The scheduler responded by enforcing token-level soft throttles and refusing some long-sequence requests.

Data sources & notes:
- telemetry.kv_cache_evictions (timeseries events per host; fields below)
- telemetry.request_queue (enqueue/dequeue timestamps, queue reason tags)
- telemetry.gpu_utilization (per-gpu sampled at 30s)
- telemetry.token_throttle (per-request token throttle events)
- logs.serving-runtime (release tag + flags)
- deployment history: serving-runtime v1.18.3 -> v1.19.0 on 2026-11-15 01:55 UTC (rollout staggered across regions)

Important field definitions (flattened):
- event_ts: ISO timestamp of event
- host_id: internal host id
- region: region tag (us-west1/eu-central1/us-east1/etc)
- model: model identifier + variant (e.g., redwood-v1-13b/q8fa)
- seq_len: sequence length observed for the request (input + output tokens)
- kv_eviction_count: number of KV entries evicted in prior 10m window on host
- kv_miss_rate: percent of KV lookups that were cold misses in prior 1m
- queue_depth: instantaneous queue depth at enqueue time
- time_in_queue_ms: ms spent waiting before GPU scheduled
- gpu_busy_pct: sampled GPU busy percent
- throttle_tokens: number of tokens soft-throttled for request
- request_id, trace_id: identifiers for cross-correlation

Representative queries used (BigQuery-like SQL):
1) Eviction spike timeseries (per region, 1m rollup):
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_ts, MINUTE) AS minute,
  region,
  COUNTIF(kv_eviction_count > 0) AS hosts_with_evictions,
  AVG(kv_eviction_count) AS avg_evictions,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(kv_miss_rate, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS kv_miss_p95
FROM telemetry.kv_cache_evictions
WHERE event_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-11-15T00:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-11-15T12:00:00Z')
GROUP BY minute, region
ORDER BY minute

2) Correlate queue depth with eviction spikes (join on minute+host_id):
SELECT
  q.minute,
  q.region,
  AVG(q.queue_depth) AS avg_queue_depth,
  AVG(e.avg_evictions) AS avg_evictions,
  SUM(t.throttle_tokens) AS total_throttled_tokens
FROM (
  -- queue rollup
  SELECT TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_ts, MINUTE) minute, host_id, region, AVG(queue_depth) queue_depth
  FROM telemetry.request_queue
  WHERE event_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-11-15T02:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-11-15T07:00:00Z')
  GROUP BY minute, host_id, region
) q
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_ts, MINUTE) minute, host_id, region, AVG(kv_eviction_count) avg_evictions
  FROM telemetry.kv_cache_evictions
  GROUP BY minute, host_id, region
) e ON q.minute = e.minute AND q.host_id = e.host_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(event_ts, MINUTE) minute, host_id, region, SUM(throttle_tokens) throttle_tokens
  FROM telemetry.token_throttle
  GROUP BY minute, host_id, region
) t ON q.minute = t.minute AND q.host_id = t.host_id
GROUP BY q.minute, q.region
ORDER BY q.minute

3) Slice on long-context requests that saw eviction-driven slowdowns:
SELECT r.request_id, r.event_ts, r.region, r.seq_len, r.time_in_queue_ms, e.kv_miss_rate, g.gpu_busy_pct
FROM telemetry.requests r
LEFT JOIN telemetry.kv_cache_evictions e ON r.host_id = e.host_id AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(r.event_ts, e.event_ts, SECOND) BETWEEN 0 AND 60
LEFT JOIN telemetry.gpu_utilization g ON r.host_id = g.host_id AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(r.event_ts, g.event_ts, SECOND) BETWEEN 0 AND 30
WHERE r.seq_len >= 1024
  AND r.event_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-11-15T02:00:00Z') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-11-15T07:00:00Z')
ORDER BY r.event_ts
LIMIT 1000

Example aggregated findings (from runs against the dataset):
- us-west1: p95 kv_miss_rate climbed from 2.1% baseline to 34.7% at 02:20 UTC; hosts_with_evictions increased from 4 -> 48 in 15m.
- eu-central1: average time_in_queue_ms for seq_len >= 2048 rose from 120ms -> 820ms between 02:15-02:50 UTC.
- total throttled tokens (global): ~2.1M tokens in incident window; 70% attributed to requests with seq_len > 1024.
- GPU busy percent across affected hosts did not saturate linearly (avg ~76%) — scheduling stalls rather than pure GPU utilization suggests sync/CPU-side KV recompute overhead.

Sample output rows (tab-separated, example):
2026-11-15T02:21:10Z	host-0932	us-west1	redwood-v1-13b/q8fa	2048	5	0.41	12	820	83	128	req-0a1b2c
(columns: event_ts, host_id, region, model, seq_len, kv_eviction_count, kv_miss_rate, queue_depth, time_in_queue_ms, gpu_busy_pct, throttle_tokens, request_id)

Anomalies & signals that mattered:
- Rapid regional spike in kv_eviction_count concurrent with deployment rollout windows for v1.19.0.
- Hosts that had recently rotated (kernel update + runtime restart) showed a larger delta in kv_miss_rate — indicates warm-state loss on restart exacerbates problem.
- Minor increase in short-duration GC pauses on affected hosts in logs.serving-runtime around cluster-auto-update timeframe.
- No corresponding increase in raw GPU memory pressure; eviction seems policy-driven (retention TTL) rather than memory OOM.

Root cause (evidence-backed):
1) v1.19.0 changed the default KV retention heuristic (lowered TTL/retention for entries created by long-context sessions) — confirmed in PR 2245.
2) During rollout some hosts restarted and lost warm caches; new heuristic prevented quick repopulation for frequently-accessed long-context prefixes, increasing backend recompute rate.
3) Increased recompute work raised CPU-side latency and serialized GPU scheduling, leading to queue growth and soft throttles to keep tail latency bounded.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled back retention change on 2026-11-15 03:45 UTC for us-west1 and eu-central1 (hotfix: revert PR 2245).
- Temporarily increased per-host in-memory KV capacity by 20% (config override) for affected regions to reduce evictions.
- Enabled aggressive proactive prefix prefetch for long-context requests in a canary group (to repopulate hot prefixes).

Follow-ups & items for postmortem:
- Engineering: add a pre-deploy simulation that measures cold-kv miss amplification for representative long-context workloads (owner: Miguel Santos, due: 2026-11-25).
- Product: update rollout checklist to include KV retention change gating and phased canary thresholds (owner: Lena Park, due: 2026-11-22).
- Infra: introduce a synthetic KV warmup job that applies to hosts post-restart to avoid warm-state loss (owner: Tomoko Yamada, due: 2026-12-05).
- Observability: create alert for sustained kv_miss_rate > 10% across >10 hosts in a region for >10 minutes, and a dashboard tile showing kv_miss_rate x queue_depth correlation (owner: Ravi Menon, due: 2026-11-23).

Quick validation checks (how to re-run this extract locally):
1) Run query (1) to get minute rollups and export CSV for the incident window.
2) Overlay per-region deployment events (from deployment history) to confirm temporal alignment.
3) Run query (2) and pivot on host groups that were part of the rollout windows to validate correlation between avg_evictions and avg_queue_depth.

Notes and caveats:
- Sampling artifacts: telemetry.gpu_utilization is sampled at 30s and may undercount short spikes. Use request-level scheduling traces for exact scheduling latency.
- Attribution: token_throttle counts are conservative; some soft-throttles were applied at the routing layer and don't emit token_throttle for fully aborted requests.
- This extract focuses on KV-level signals; additional investigation required for scheduler internals (SRE) and kernel update side-effects.

Appendix: quick list of useful queries (names refer to internal saved queries):
- q_kv_eviction_minute_rollup_incident_window
- q_queue_vs_eviction_join_incident_window
- q_long_context_slow_requests_kv_join
- q_host_restart_and_kv_warmth

Owners & points-of-contact:
- Incident lead: Asha Rao (eng-infrastructure)
- Runtime owner: Miguel Santos (serving-runtime)
- SRE contact: Tomoko Yamada (site-reliability)

End of extract.
